title: AWS CWI Training in Fort Worth, TX: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Fort Worth aerospace, rail, bridge and pipeline welders: corporate at your plant, self-paced online or one-to-one.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Fort Worth: Six Days for Aerospace, Rail and Highway Welding Inspectors
html:
Fort Worth's welding work leans toward things that fly, roll and carry traffic. Fighter jets come off the assembly line at Air Force Plant 4, Bell is setting up a new components plant for the Army's next assault aircraft, BNSF Railway runs its network from a headquarters in the city, and the Southeast Connector is rebuilding dozens of highway bridges across Tarrant County. Behind those names sit hundreds of machine shops, fabricators and repair yards whose welds somebody has to accept. Atlantis NDT runs a six-day (6-day) course that prepares Fort Worth welders, fitters, QC staff and engineers for the American Welding Society's Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination. You can take it as a corporate course at your employer's site, study online at your own pace with an instructor on call for questions, or book one-to-one sessions online or in person. AWS administers the examination and is the only body that grants the CWI; the course does not certify anyone and carries no AWS approval or endorsement. There is no Atlantis classroom in Fort Worth. To talk through your situation, send a Fort Worth CWI exam prep enquiry.

What the six days cover, in any of the three formats

The course is built around the three parts of the AWS exam. The opening two days work through Part A Fundamentals: arc welding processes, terms from AWS A3.0, joint geometry, welding symbols under A2.4, metallurgy, destructive and nondestructive testing, discontinuities and their causes, safety and the arithmetic inspectors use. Day three is practical preparation for Part B, built on measuring welds and reading procedure documents. Day four is code application in your chosen book. Day five is timed practice papers, and day six returns to the topics you missed and to exam logistics. The full six-day outline sits on the national page.

  • Corporate: the six days delivered at a Fort Worth-area employer's facility for a group of its people, using the company's own welds, gauges and, where it fits, its code and procedures.
  • Online: a study plan that follows the six-day outline, with course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, plus an instructor who answers questions as you go. There are no class times to keep.
  • One-to-one: six days of sessions between one candidate and the instructor, held online or in person at a location agreed when the booking is made.

The practice material is Atlantis's own work, written against the subject areas AWS publishes. It reproduces nothing from the AWS examination, and Atlantis cannot see the exam or any candidate's results.

Fort Worth's welding economy, sector by sector

Military aircraft at Air Force Plant 4

Lockheed Martin assembles the F-35 at Air Force Plant 4 on the west side of the city, on a production line long enough that visitors describe it in miles. Much of a modern fighter's airframe is machined, composite and fastened rather than welded, so the welding inspection in this supply chain concentrates in the suppliers: shops making ducts, tubing, brackets, engine-related hardware, test rigs, tooling and ground support equipment. Those welds are small, often in titanium, stainless or nickel alloys, and inspected against weld classes and customer specifications with strict traceability. A CWI in that environment proves broad welding knowledge, and the employer adds training on its own specifications.

Rotorcraft and the Bell expansion

Bell has called Texas home for more than six decades and describes itself as one of the largest aerospace employers in North Texas. In late 2024 it chose a Fort Worth building for a new facility that will make components for the Army's Future Long Range Assault Aircraft, with production scheduled to start in 2028. New aerospace programs pull in welding suppliers, process qualifications and inspectors well before the first part ships, so the next few years are a sensible time for a Tarrant County aerospace welder to move toward inspection.

Railroads, Alliance and the logistics corridor

BNSF Railway's headquarters is in Fort Worth, and its Alliance intermodal facility in the north of the city has anchored the AllianceTexas logistics district for three decades. Railcars and locomotives are welded and repaired to their own rules, and AWS D15.1, the Railroad Welding Specification for Cars and Locomotives, is one of the Part C books AWS offers. Track and rail joint welding is a different discipline governed by railroad standards, so a D15.1 choice makes sense for people in car and locomotive shops rather than track gangs.

Highway bridges and the Southeast Connector

The Southeast Connector is rebuilding about fourteen miles of I-820, I-20 and US 287 through southeast Tarrant County and Arlington, and the City of Arlington reports that it includes reconstructing or rehabilitating 61 bridges. The project is described as the largest transportation investment in the history of TxDOT's Fort Worth District, with substantial completion expected in early 2028. Where structures like these use steel members, the fabricator works to AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, which is stricter than D1.1 on procedure qualification, consumable control and fracture-critical members.

Pipelines, tanks and the Barnett Shale

Fort Worth sits on top of the Barnett Shale, and gathering lines, compressor stations and storage tanks are part of the landscape around the city. AWS chose Fort Worth to host its 2025 Pipeline, Related Facilities, and Tanks Conference, a fair sign of how much of that industry works from here. Pipeline welding is usually specified to API 1104; storage tanks follow their own API standards, which are not among the CWI exam books.

Buildings, warehouses and industrial steel

Distribution centers along the I-35W and Alliance corridors, hospital and office projects, and industrial buildings bring structural steel welded under AWS D1.1 and checked under the building code's special inspection rules. Testing agencies and fabricators across Tarrant County keep CWIs on staff for that work, in the shop and on site.

Who employs welding inspectors in Tarrant County

  • Aerospace suppliers need inspectors comfortable with weld classes, process sheets and first-article paperwork. Expect questions about specifications and records as much as about welds.
  • Rail car and locomotive repair shops want people who know how repairs are qualified and documented, and who can spot cracking at attachments, bolsters and underframe connections.
  • Bridge and structural fabricators hire D1.5 and D1.1 inspectors to control preheat, welder qualification and visual acceptance before steel ships.
  • Testing agencies supply special inspectors for buildings and highway work across the Metroplex.
  • Midstream operators and pipeline contractors staff API 1104 inspectors for Barnett Shale gathering and station projects.

Employers here often list the CWI as required for QC lead roles and as preferred for technicians. For what the credential tends to mean for pay and progression, read CWI requirements and career impact.

Matching the Part C code to Fort Worth work

AWS lets you pick the open-book code when you apply. The list includes D1.1 structural steel, API 1104 pipelines, D1.2 aluminum, D1.5 bridges, D15.1 railcars and locomotives, D17.1 aerospace fusion welding, the ASME option of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. In Fort Worth, four different books each have a real local following.

Your Fort Worth workBook to considerWhat you will practise
Aerospace supplier welding, tooling and test hardwareAWS D17.1Weld classes, inspection requirements and acceptance limits per class
Railcar or locomotive repair and manufactureAWS D15.1Qualification, workmanship and inspection rules for cars and locomotives
Steel bridge fabrication for TxDOT or toll agenciesAWS D1.5Qualified procedures, consumable control, fracture-critical requirements
Buildings, warehouses, industrial steelAWS D1.1Prequalified joints, tolerances, visual acceptance
Gathering lines, stations, transmission tie-insAPI 1104Procedure and welder qualification, field acceptance standards

If you split time between buildings and bridges, D1.1 is usually the more flexible first book, with D1.5 learned on the job afterward. Always study the edition AWS names for the exam rather than the newest copy in the shop. Background: AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5 and API 1104.

AWS sections and welding schools serving Fort Worth

AWS lists its local sections on aws.org/sections. In North Texas, the section with an active published calendar that we could confirm is the North Texas Section, part of District 17, whose recent technical meetings featured welding instructors from Dallas College and a local high school welding program. San Antonio, Corpus Christi and the Sabine area sit in District 18. Use the section finder to see which section covers your address, then go to a meeting: it is the easiest way to find working inspectors who can confirm your welding history for the AWS application.

Many Fort Worth welders trained at Tarrant County College. Its welding program runs at the Northwest Campus beside Alliance Airport, inside the college's Erma C. Johnson Hadley Center of Excellence for Aviation, Transportation and Logistics, and students there have welded stainless high-pressure lines for boiler applications as part of their coursework. Some area school districts also offer dual-credit welding classes. These programs are part of the local talent pipeline; they are not Atlantis partners or venues.

Booking the CWI exam from Fort Worth

After AWS approves your application, its confirmation letter gives you an eligibility code. Prometric asks for that code when you schedule the two computer-based parts: Part A, 150 questions on fundamentals, and Part C, roughly 50 to 65 questions answered with your code book open. Prometric's site lists the centers nearest Tarrant County.

The practical is arranged separately. AWS gives Part B at its own seminar and exam locations, combining hands-on tasks using tools and specimens AWS supplies with 46 questions. AWS publishes CWI location pages for several Texas cities, among them Austin, Houston, San Antonio, Corpus Christi and Beaumont, so check the seminar and exam schedule for the session that is easiest to reach and expect some driving. AWS requires at least 72% on every part and lists its examination fees on aws.org. To plan the whole outlay, including time off and the code book, see the CWI exam budget guide.

Fitting study around aerospace shifts, rail call-outs and night closures

Fort Worth employers keep awkward hours. Aerospace plants run multiple production shifts behind security gates, rail repair crews get called out when cars are set out, and highway contractors pour and erect at night when lanes are closed. The online format suits all three, because nothing happens at a fixed time and questions go to the instructor whenever they arise. A sensible plan is to cover the fundamentals over several weeks, carry your chosen code book and practise finding clauses that apply to the welds in front of you, then sit the timed practice papers in the two weeks before your Prometric appointment.

For Part B, practise measuring until the gauge readings come without thinking: fillet leg and throat, convexity and concavity, undercut depth and joint misalignment. Use scrap, test coupons and cut-outs, write each number before judging it, and compare it with a written acceptance limit. The welding workshop simulator in Practical NDT helps you rehearse inspection sequences when you are away from the shop.

Corporate delivery at a Fort Worth plant, shop or yard

A company preparing several people can bring the six days inside its own fence. That matters in aerospace, where visitors and devices are controlled and taking a group off site costs a shift. An aerospace supplier can run the code day in D17.1, a rail shop in D15.1, and a structural fabricator in D1.1 or D1.5; a mixed group can split the code day so each person works in the book they will choose.

The practical day uses the employer's own gauges and real welds, from welder test plates to rejected production parts, so measurement practice matches the joints those inspectors will accept. Dates are agreed around production and outages. Each candidate still applies to AWS personally, with their own experience record and vision examination; an employer cannot submit those for them.

One-to-one sessions, online or in person

A single candidate can book the six days as one-to-one time with the instructor. Online suits someone working rotating aerospace shifts; in person takes place at a location agreed when booking, such as the candidate's workplace, because there is still no Atlantis classroom in the city. People often choose this format after a near miss on one part, or when moving from a welding booth into a QC role with a fixed exam date. Read how candidates fare on Parts A, B and C to see where focused time usually pays off.

Eligibility and the vision record

AWS weighs schooling against welding-related experience. With a high school diploma you need five years; with an associate degree in an engineering technology, engineering or physical science field, two; with a bachelor's in welding engineering or welding technology, one. AWS alone decides whether a particular TCC certificate or degree counts toward a shorter route. You also need an AWS Visual Acuity Record showing near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, corrected or not, and a color perception test, done by a qualified practitioner within the window AWS allows before the exam. Candidates who are short of the experience can start with the Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI). The complete table is on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

Career paths after the CWI in Fort Worth

AWS keeps the CWI valid for nine years, with renewals due at years three and six and recertification at nine. In Fort Worth the next move usually follows the industry you are in.

  • Aerospace: many inspectors add nondestructive testing so they can run penetrant, magnetic particle or ultrasonic checks themselves. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies NDT staff after training and logged method hours, and Atlantis provides the training; see aerospace NDT training and ultrasonic testing in aviation.
  • Rail: inspectors in car and locomotive shops often add magnetic particle or ultrasonic methods; see magnetic particle testing in rail.
  • Structural and bridge work: the Senior CWI (SCWI) and AWS endorsements widen the codes you are recognized on; see the Senior CWI pathway.
  • Core skills: VT Level 2 training deepens the visual technique at the heart of the CWI; see also visual testing and weld inspection services.

To compare credentials, read AWS CWI vs API 577 vs ASNT Level II. Local pages: NDT training in Fort Worth, ultrasonic testing in Fort Worth, third-party inspection in Fort Worth and the Practical NDT simulator for Fort Worth.

Nearby CWI pages and how to request a quote

For the wider region, see the CWI exam prep pages for Dallas, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, San Antonio and Houston.

To get a quote, tell us the format (corporate, online or one-to-one), the number of candidates, an outline of each person's schooling and welding work, and the Part C book each intends to take. For corporate delivery, include the site address, any access rules, the gauges and sample welds available and the weeks to avoid. Send it through the Fort Worth CWI enquiry form. The course is priced on request; AWS sets and publishes its own exam fees.

faq.q: Does Atlantis teach the CWI course in a Fort Worth classroom?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Fort Worth. You can study online with an instructor answering your questions, book six one-to-one days online or in person at an agreed location, or have your employer host the six days on site. See the outline.

faq.q: Who grants the CWI after I finish the course?
faq.a: AWS. It checks your eligibility, runs Parts A, B and C, and issues the certification if you pass. The six days prepare you; Atlantis certifies no one and the course is not AWS-approved or endorsed.

faq.q: Which Part C book suits an aerospace supplier in Fort Worth?
faq.a: AWS D17.1, the aerospace fusion welding specification, is the natural fit for people welding or inspecting aerospace hardware. If your job is mostly tooling bases or structural support steel, D1.1 can be the better choice.

faq.q: I work in a railcar repair shop. Is there a code for me?
faq.a: Yes. AWS offers D15.1, the Railroad Welding Specification for Cars and Locomotives, as a Part C option. It covers car and locomotive work, not track welding.

faq.q: Which book should a bridge fabricator supplying TxDOT work choose?
faq.a: AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, if bridge steel is your daily work. See AWS D1.5. People who move between buildings and bridges often take D1.1 first.

faq.q: Where do Fort Worth candidates sit the exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are booked with Prometric using the eligibility code from your AWS confirmation letter. Part B is run by AWS at its seminar locations; AWS lists several Texas cities, so check its schedule and expect to travel.

faq.q: Is one-to-one available in person in Fort Worth?
faq.a: Yes, at a location agreed when you book, such as your workplace. The same six days can also run as one-to-one sessions online, which suits rotating shifts.

faq.q: Can an aerospace plant keep its group on site for the course?
faq.a: Yes. Corporate delivery brings all six days inside your facility, uses your gauges and welds, and can split the code day by book. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually. Request a quote.

faq.q: Do the practice papers contain AWS exam questions?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes all practice questions and timed papers itself, following the subject areas AWS publishes, and has no access to the AWS examination.

faq.q: Can I add NDT methods after the CWI?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training in VT, MT, PT and UT; your employer certifies you under its written practice. See NDT training in Fort Worth.
